content.title: 6.3 Reperfusion treatment — 6.3.1 Systemic thrombolysis
content.summary: Thrombolytic therapy for pulmonary embolism (PE) leads to faster improvements in pulmonary obstruction, PAP and PVR, and reduces RV dilation compared with UFH alone. Greatest benefit is when treatment is started within 48 h of symptom onset, but may be useful up to ~14 days. Unsuccessful thrombolysis (persistent instability/unchanged RV dysfunction) reported in ~8% of high-risk PE. Meta-analyses show reduced mortality/recurrent PE but increased bleeding (≈9.9% severe bleeding; 1.7% intracranial haemorrhage). In intermediate‑risk PE (RV dysfunction + elevated troponin) thrombolysis reduced haemodynamic decompensation but increased extracranial/intracranial bleeding (PEITHO trial).
content.recommended_regimens_and_dosing: Accelerated IV administration of recombinant tissue‑type plasminogen activator (rtPA; 100 mg over 2 h) is preferred to prolonged infusions of first‑generation agents (streptokinase, urokinase). Reduced‑dose rtPA reports need confirmation. UFH may be given during continuous infusion of alteplase but should be discontinued during infusion of streptokinase or urokinase.
content.investigational_agents: Reteplase, desmoteplase and tenecteplase have been investigated for acute PE but are not currently approved for this indication.
content.safety_considerations: Thrombolysis is associated with increased risk of severe extracranial and intracranial bleeding; intracranial haemorrhage rate ~1.7% in trials. Contraindications and detailed regimens are listed in Table 10 (referenced).
content.references_and_trials: PEITHO trial evaluated thrombolysis in intermediate‑risk PE. Meta-analyses and several supplementary tables referenced for detailed outcomes and contraindications.

Associated Conditions: Use in systemic thrombolysis / thrombolytic therapy
genes.context: Recombinant tissue‑type plasminogen activator (rtPA; 100 mg over 2 h), alteplase, reteplase and tenecteplase (all tPA derivatives) are discussed as thrombolytic agents for acute PE; accelerated IV rtPA preferred to prolonged infusions.
Urokinase (urokinase‑type plasminogen activator) is listed among first‑generation thrombolytic agents (streptokinase and urokinase) and discussed regarding infusion and UFH coadministration.

Associated Conditions: Target of plasminogen activators in thrombolytic therapy
genes.context: The term 'plasminogen' appears in 'tissue‑type plasminogen activator' (rtPA), indicating the substrate (plasminogen) for thrombolytic agents used in PE treatment.
